name: Facet
text:
Adopt a **system-wide dark theme by default** with **no light mode toggle**, but include a **persistent system preference sync** that respects the user’s OS-level theme setting.

Dark mode cuts glare and eye strain in low light, matching our clarity and focus goals. Forcing consistency avoids mid-task fragmentation, while syncing with OS settings removes the need for manual toggles—users get their preferred theme automatically. The trade-off is excluding users who manually override their OS theme, but most light-sensitive users already use system-level dark mode, so this covers the majority without extra UI.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Auto-adjusting based on time-of-day or glare risks misfiring—users in dim offices at noon or bright rooms at night get the wrong theme, creating more friction than a static toggle. A better alternative is a persistent, system-wide default with a **persistent, high-contrast light mode toggle** that’s always visible, not hidden in settings—settle it by measuring task completion time for light-sensitive users in both modes.
